Reproducing Hunt, Malalasekera et al. (2018) from CRCNS pfc-7¶

Paper: Hunt, Malalasekera, de Berker, Miranda, Farmer, Behrens & Kennerley (2018), "Triple dissociation of attention and decision computations across prefrontal cortex", Nature Neuroscience 21, 1471-1481, doi:10.1038/s41593-018-0239-5.

Data: CRCNS data set pfc-7 (doi:10.6080/K0PZ5712), read anonymously from the public S3 bucket crcnsarchive under pfc-7/live/. CRCNS data sets are not versioned, so the version is recorded as unversioned; the only published copy is the one under live/ (data description version 0.5, September 6, 2018), and it is the one pinned here. The MD5 sums of the files read, from the data set's checksums.md5, are printed below, so that a later change is detectable.

Claims: claims/hunt-2018.yaml, written from the version of record (PMC6331040) with its supplement. The paper's MATLAB scripts are files of the data set (scripts.zip); where the claims file leaves a detail open and a script settles it, the script is cited (see pfc7.py).

All 40 claims of the claims file are tested; none is blocked. Outcomes are in the summary at the end.

    """One generator per claim section, seeded from its name (a standard choice)."""
    return np.random.default_rng(zlib.crc32(name.encode()))

Loading¶

The file listing and checksums, the units table, the two behavioural files (one at a time, in memory), and the preprocessed units of ACC, DLPFC and OFC (reduced as they load).

In [2]:

md5 = pfc7.checksums()

The GLM written here (pfc7.fit_glm) is checked against the T-statistics the authors stored in neuronal_regression_results/info_gathering_cue123_alltrials_attentional_final.mat, which the data set's scripts load for Figures 5 to 7. This checks the implementation; no result below uses the stored values.

Clock check¶

Every stream shares the clock of the trial table: the cue 1 rasters are cut from each trial's spike times at the cue 1 onset code, the GLM T-statistic for the attended cue 1 value (EVs 1 + 5) rises only after cue 1 onset, and with the trial labels shifted by one trial the response vanishes. The contrast is shown for OFC, the region with the strongest value code.

In [5]:
ofc_sel = [u for u in U if int(U[u]["brain_region"]) == 3 and info.loc[u, "info_rate"] >= 1 and u != 87]
def mean_abs_t(shift):
    out = []
    for u in ofc_sel:
        d = dict(U[u])
        if shift:
            for k in ["reg_mat", "condition", "attendsac1", "Left_choice", "num_pics_viewed"]:
                d[k] = np.roll(d[k], shift, axis=0)
        out.append(np.abs(pfc7.fit_glm(d, epochs=("X1",), halves=False)["tX1"][18]))
    return np.mean(out, axis=0)
clk = pd.DataFrame({"true labels": mean_abs_t(0), "labels shifted 1 trial": mean_abs_t(1)},
                   index=pfc7.TIMEBINS)
print("mean |T| of cue 1 value across OFC neurons, by bin centre (ms after cue 1):")
print(clk.iloc[::5].round(2).T)

Lines of the paper's scripts cited here¶

The scripts are a file of the data set (scripts.zip). The lines below are read from it, so that the details taken from them can be checked: the unit exclusions (units 87 and 653), the one-sided RSA permutation test, the variables stacked for Supplementary Figure 5C (the rt numbering: 3 stimulus identity, 4 attended value, 5 accept/reject, 6 spatial attention, 7 left/right value; areas 1 ACC, 2 DLPFC, 3 OFC) and the 10% peak CPD rule, the cluster test of Figure 5g-j, the response bin of the Figure 6 action weights (index 30, centred 210 ms before the response) and the per-unit random halves, the Figure 7 thresholds, and the Figure 8 binomial formula.

Unit selection¶

Units in ACC, DLPFC and OFC with mean rate of at least 1 Hz. The paper's scripts take the rate from all_units_info.mat and also drop unit 87 (Fig4_RSA.m and the other figure scripts) and, for Figures 5 and 7, unit 653. That is the selection used below (SEL, SEL5); the claim neuron-counts compares the counts under the claims file's readings of the rate.

In [7]:
base = info[info.area.isin([1, 2, 3])].copy()
base["session_rate"] = [U[u]["rate_session"] for u in base.index]
base["trial_rate"] = [U[u]["rate_trials"] for u in base.index]
keep = (base.info_rate >= 1) & ~base.index.isin(pfc7.BAD_UNITS)
SEL = {a: base.index[keep & (base.area == a)].tolist() for a in (1, 2, 3)}
SEL5 = {a: [u for u in SEL[a] if u not in pfc7.NAN_TSTAT_UNITS] for a in (1, 2, 3)}
print({pfc7.AREAS[a]: len(v) for a, v in SEL.items()}, "Figures 5 and 7:",
      {pfc7.AREAS[a]: len(v) for a, v in SEL5.items()})
NAMES = pfc7.AREAS

sessions-and-trials¶

Behaviour comes from 25 sessions of monkey F and 32 of monkey M, 9,863 trials for F and 14,251 for M.

The behavioural files hold only completed option and attribute trials (trial errors 0 and 6), so reading (a) is their trial count. Aborted trials are counted from the full trial lists (BhvInfo) in the unit files, which exist only for sessions with units; reading (c) drops trials of equal expected value. "Miles" is M and "Frank" is F (the unit files' sb field and the data descriptor's naming).

Result: reproduced. The behavioural files hold 25 sessions of monkey F (Frank) and 32 of monkey M (Miles), with 9,863 and 14,251 completed option and attribute trials, the paper's counts exactly under reading (a). Reading (c) gives 9,479 and 13,691; reading (b) can be counted only for the 24 and 29 sessions with units (10,688 and 14,391 trials there).

The data set holds 198 ACC, 156 DLPFC and 195 OFC units over 24 F and 29 M sessions, the totals and session counts the claims file derives from Supplementary Table 1. With the average_firing_rate of all_units_info.mat, which every figure script uses to select units, 189 ACC, 135 DLPFC and 183 OFC units are at or above 1 Hz, and 9, 21 and 12 are excluded, as the paper says. Neither of the claims file's readings gives these counts: the whole-session rate gives 190, 136 and 182, the trial rate 186, 137 and 179. The scripts also drop unit 87 (DLPFC), so the analyses here, as the paper's, use 134 DLPFC units. Session by session, Supplementary Table 1 agrees with the data in all 53 sessions and all three areas when every unit is counted, and in only 26 of 53 when units below 1 Hz are left out, so the table counts all units although its caption says units above 1 Hz.

choice-accuracy-ev¶

Monkeys F and M chose the option with the higher expected value on 76.6% and 79.8% of trials.

In [10]:
def acc_ev(b, ties):
    hi_left = b.LEV > b.REV
    eq = b.LEV == b.REV
    corr = (hi_left & (b.left_choice == 1)) | (~hi_left & ~eq & (b.left_choice == 0))
    if ties == "out":
        return 100 * corr[~eq].mean()
    if ties == "wrong":
        return 100 * corr.mean()
    return 100 * (corr | eq).mean()   # InfoGathering_Behaviour.m counts ties as correct
r = pd.DataFrame({t: beh.groupby("subject").apply(acc_ev, ties=t) for t in ["out", "wrong", "right"]})
r.columns = ["(a) ties left out", "(b) ties counted wrong", "script: ties counted right"]
print(r.round(2))
print("ties:", beh[beh.LEV == beh.REV].groupby("subject").size().to_dict())
print("expected F 76.6 +/- 7.66, M 79.8 +/- 7.98")

      .groupby(level=0).agg(["min", "median", "max"]).round(1).to_dict("index"))

chose-on-partial-information¶

Monkeys F and M chose before seeing all four cues on 85.5% and 71.4% of trials.

The claims file gives no method. InfoGathering_Behaviour.m counts a trial as an early choice when, after correcting the number of pictures for a joystick movement made before the last picture was fixated (num_pics_viewedprezero), fewer than four were viewed (out.earlychoices = 1 - mean(num_pics_viewedprezero==4)); that is taken here, and the raw count of fixated pictures is shown too.

Result: reproduced, resting on an assumption. With the script's joystick-corrected count, F chose before all four cues on 85.52% and M on 71.43% of trials (paper 85.5% and 71.4%). The paper does not define "evaluated", and the outcome depends on the definition: the raw count of fixated pictures gives 54.23% and 42.56%, outside the tolerance, and the 250 ms rule gives 95.59% and 92.25%, outside it too. The script's count (InfoGathering_Behaviour.m, out.earlychoices) is taken as the paper's definition.

choice-accuracy-observed¶

Judged by the pictures observed, choice accuracy was 86.3% for monkey F and 87.4% for monkey M.

Which pictures count as observed is taken from InfoGathering_Behaviour.m (accuracy_seen): those fixated before the joystick moved, dropping a last picture fixated for 250 ms or less (num_pics_viewed250). The script also sets unseen cues to 0.5, shifts magnitudes by -0.05 and counts ties as correct; that is shown as a variant.

In [12]:
def acc_seen(b, npv_col, reading):
    if reading == "script":
        v = pfc7.seen_values(b, npv_col, unseen=(0.5, 0.5), mag_shift=True)
        L, R = v[:, 0] * v[:, 1], v[:, 2] * v[:, 3]
        ties = "right"
    elif reading in ("a", "b"):
        v = pfc7.seen_values(b, npv_col, unseen=(0.5, 0.55), mag_shift=False)
        L, R = v[:, 0] * v[:, 1], v[:, 2] * v[:, 3]
        ties = "out" if reading == "a" else "wrong"
    else:  # (c) sum of the observed ranks per option
        L = np.zeros(len(b)); R = np.zeros(len(b))
        for k, row in enumerate(b.itertuples()):
            n = getattr(row, npv_col)
            for rk, lf in zip(row.seq_rank[:n], row.seq_left[:n]):
                if lf:
                    L[k] += rk
                else:
                    R[k] += rk
        ties = "out"
    L = np.round(L, 6); R = np.round(R, 6)
    lc = b.left_choice.values == 1
    eq = L == R
    corr = ((L > R) & lc) | ((R > L) & ~lc)
    if ties == "out":
        return 100 * corr[~eq].mean()
    if ties == "wrong":
        return 100 * corr.mean()
    return 100 * (corr | eq).mean()
rows = {}
for npv_col in ["npv250", "npv"]:
    for rd in ["a", "b", "c", "script"]:
        rows[(npv_col, rd)] = beh.groupby("subject").apply(acc_seen, npv_col=npv_col, reading=rd)
aso = pd.DataFrame(rows).T
aso.index.names = ["pictures seen", "reading"]
print(aso.round(2))

figs1ab-cue-weights¶

In logistic regressions of choice, both monkeys weighted reward probability and magnitude about equally and used all four viewed cues, with a slight upweighting of the antepenultimate (n-2) cue, and both showed a small bias towards choosing the second side on option trials.

Model B follows InfoGathering_Behaviour.m (choice on left minus right seen probability and seen magnitude, unseen at 0.5, with a constant and a first-side term, separately for option and attribute trials, no further constant). Model A regresses choice on a constant and the final, n-1, n-2 and n-3 viewed pictures, signed + left and - right (the script uses lastLreg - lastRreg on the pictures fixated).

In [13]:
def model_b(b, seen=True):
    if seen:
        v = pfc7.seen_values(b, "npv250", unseen=(0.5, 0.5), mag_shift=True)
        dp, dm = v[:, 0] - v[:, 2], v[:, 1] - v[:, 3]
    else:
        dp, dm = (b.LP - b.RP).values, (b.LM - b.RM).values
    fs = np.array([r.seq_left[0] for r in b.itertuples()], float)
    base_ = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(b)), dp, dm, fs])
    X = np.hstack([base_ * (b.condition.values == 3)[:, None], base_ * (b.condition.values == 4)[:, None]])
    res = sm.GLM(b.left_choice.values, X, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit()
    names = [f"{t} {n}" for t in ("option", "attribute") for n in ("left bias", "prob", "mag", "first side")]
    out = pd.DataFrame({"b": res.params, "se": res.bse, "p": res.pvalues}, index=names)
    waldp = {}
    for t, o in (("option", 0), ("attribute", 4)):
        c = np.zeros(8); c[o + 1] = 1; c[o + 2] = -1
        w = res.t_test(c)
        waldp[t] = float(w.pvalue)
    return out, waldp
def model_a(b, scale):
    Xs = np.zeros((len(b), 4))
    for k, r in enumerate(b.itertuples()):
        n = r.npv
        for j in range(min(n, 4)):
            idx = n - 1 - j
            rk = r.seq_rank[idx]
            val = rk if scale == "rank" else (0.1 + 0.2 * (rk + 2))
            Xs[k, j] = val if r.seq_left[idx] else -val
    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(b)), Xs])
    res = sm.GLM(b.left_choice.values, X, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit()
    return pd.DataFrame({"b": res.params, "se": res.bse, "p": res.pvalues},
                        index=["left bias", "final", "n-1", "n-2", "n-3"])
S1 = {}
for sb in ["F", "M"]:
    b = beh[beh.subject == sb]
    for seen in (True, False):
        mb, wp = model_b(b, seen)
        ci = mb.b.values[:, None] + np.array([-1.96, 1.96]) * mb.se.values[:, None]
        print(f"--- {sb}, model B, {'seen values (script)' if seen else 'true values'}")
        print(mb.round(4))
        for t, o in (("option", 0), ("attribute", 4)):
            ov = not (ci[o + 1, 1] < ci[o + 2, 0] or ci[o + 2, 1] < ci[o + 1, 0])
            print(f"  {t}: prob/mag ratio {mb.b.iloc[o + 1] / mb.b.iloc[o + 2]:.2f}, 95% CIs overlap {ov},"
                  f" Wald p(prob = mag) {wp[t]:.3g}")
            S1[(sb, seen, t)] = dict(pos=(mb.b.iloc[o + 1] > 0) and (mb.b.iloc[o + 2] > 0), overlap=ov, wald=wp[t])
        S1[(sb, seen, "first")] = (mb.b.iloc[3], mb.p.iloc[3])
    for scale in ("rank", "raw"):
        ma = model_a(b, scale)
        print(f"--- {sb}, model A, {scale}")
        print(ma.round(4))
        S1[(sb, "A", scale)] = ma

Result: partially reproduced. In model A every picture weight is positive with p < 0.05 in both monkeys under both scales, and the first-side term on option trials is negative in both (F b = -0.467, p = 1.5e-07; M b = -1.220, p = 2.7e-54, seen values). Equal weighting of probability and magnitude fails in M: the ratio is 1.11 on option and 1.13 on attribute trials, the 95% CIs do not overlap and the Wald test gives p = 1.1e-06 and 4.1e-07; with true values the ratios are 1.11 and 1.15 and the attribute CIs do not overlap. In F the CIs overlap on both trial types. The n-2 weight (F 1.186, M 1.161 on ranks) is below the n-1 weight (1.347, 1.229), so the slight upweighting of the antepenultimate cue is not seen against n-1; it is above the final weight.

figs1cd-fewer-cues-more-accurate¶

Choices were more often optimal on trials where 2 pictures were viewed than on trials with 3 or 4, because trials ended early when the first two cues gave a larger value difference.

The number of pictures viewed is taken from InfoGathering_Behaviour.m (num_pics_viewed250, used for Supplementary Figure 1c/d); the raw count of fixated pictures is shown too. The claims file, as amended after a reader's answer (questions/hunt-2018.yaml), allows two measures of accuracy: (A) the choice of the higher true expected value, reading (a) of choice-accuracy-ev (ties left out); (B) the choice of the higher expected value of the pictures observed, under the readings of choice-accuracy-observed. Trials are pooled over sessions; the script's mean over sessions is shown as a variant.

In [15]:
def vd_cues12(b):
    out = np.zeros(len(b))
    for k, r in enumerate(b.itertuples()):
        lp, lm, rp, rm = 0.5, 0.55, 0.5, 0.55
        for p in r.positions[:2]:
            isprob = (p in (91, 93)) == (r.prob_top == 1)
            left = p in (91, 92)
            if isprob and left: lp = r.LP
            elif isprob: rp = r.RP
            elif left: lm = r.LM
            else: rm = r.RM
        out[k] = abs(lp * lm - rp * rm)
    return out
beh["vd_true"] = (beh.LEV - beh.REV).abs()
beh["vd_12"] = vd_cues12(beh)
rows = []
for col in ["npv250", "npv"]:
    for sb in ["F", "M"]:
        b = beh[beh.subject == sb]
        for n in (2, 3, 4):
            bb = b[b[col] == n]
            rows.append(dict(count=col, subject=sb, n=n, trials=len(bb), accuracy=acc_ev(bb, "out"),
                             vd_true=bb.vd_true.mean(), vd_cues12=bb.vd_12.mean()))
s1cd = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(["count", "subject", "n"]).sort_index()
# InfoGathering_Behaviour.m (accuracyNPV, mvd): accuracy judged on the seen values (unseen 0.5,
# magnitudes shifted, ties counted right), per session, then averaged over sessions
sv = pfc7.seen_values(beh, "npv250", unseen=(0.5, 0.5), mag_shift=True)
beh["Lseen"], beh["Rseen"] = sv[:, 0] * sv[:, 1], sv[:, 2] * sv[:, 3]
beh["acc_seen"] = (((beh.Lseen >= beh.Rseen) & (beh.left_choice == 1)) | ((beh.Rseen >= beh.Lseen) & (beh.left_choice == 0)))
scr = (beh.groupby(["subject", "session", "npv250"]).agg(acc=("acc_seen", "mean"), vd=("vd_true", "mean"))
       .groupby(level=[0, 2]).mean())
print("script's measure (mean over sessions of accuracy on seen values; mean |EV difference|):")
print((scr.assign(acc=100 * scr.acc)).round(3))
print(s1cd.round(3))

Result: reproduced. Under measure (B), with trials pooled and the script's count of pictures, accuracy on 2-picture trials is the highest in both monkeys under every reading of choice-accuracy-observed: under reading (a) F 90.24% against 82.67% and 79.81% on 3 and 4 pictures, M 94.62% against 85.98% and 81.70%. The mean value difference is largest on 2-picture trials in both monkeys under both readings (true expected values, F 0.266 against 0.229 and 0.219, M 0.271 against 0.240 and 0.228). Under measure (A) accuracy on 2-picture trials is not the highest (F 74.96% against 76.10% and 79.62%; M 78.83% against 78.79% and 81.51%). The script's mean over sessions gives the same order as (B) (F 90.19% against 82.63% and 82.27%; M 93.65% against 85.20% and 83.69%). With the raw count of fixated pictures, (B) holds in both monkeys under readings (a), (c) and the script's, and in F only under (b).

fig2a-sample-the-favourite¶

On attribute trials, the free third saccade went preferentially to the option with the higher value between cue 1 and cue 2.

for sb in ["F", "M", "both"]:
    b = beh[(beh.condition == 4) & (beh.npv >= 3)]
    if sb != "both":
        b = b[b.subject == sb]
    back = np.array([r.seq_left[2] == r.seq_left[0] for r in b.itertuples()], float)
    d12 = np.array([r.seq_rank[0] - r.seq_rank[1] for r in b.itertuples()], float)
    res = sm.GLM(back, sm.add_constant(d12), family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit()
    hi1, lo1 = back[d12 > 0], back[d12 < 0]
    chi, pchi, _, _ = stats.chi2_contingency([[hi1.sum(), len(hi1) - hi1.sum()], [lo1.sum(), len(lo1) - lo1.sum()]])
    print(f"{sb}: n = {len(b)}; (a) slope on rank1 - rank2 {res.params[1]:.3f}, p = {res.pvalues[1]:.2g};"
          f" (b) back to option 1 when cue 1 > cue 2 {hi1.mean():.3f} (n={len(hi1)}), when cue 1 < cue 2"
          f" {lo1.mean():.3f} (n={len(lo1)}), chi2 = {chi:.1f}, p = {pchi:.2g}")

RSA at cue 1 (claims fig4d to fig4h, figs2, figs4, figs11)¶

Fig4_RSA.m and calculate_RSA_matrices.m: per unit the mean spike count 100 < t < 500 ms after cue 1 in each of 20 conditions, z-scored across conditions; Pearson correlation between conditions; OLS of the 400 elements on the seven columns of pfc7.rsa_design. T-statistics and the between-region F-statistics are compared with 10,000 permutations of the 20 condition labels. The script's test is one-sided (1 - mean(t > tp)), reading (a) of O8; reading (b), two-sided on |T|, is shown too. Reading (a) of O9 (all completed trials) is what calculate_RSA_matrices.m uses; reading (b) keeps trials with 3 or more cues.

In [19]:
def rsa_unitmat(units, key="rsa", field="m20"):
    return np.column_stack([U[u][key][field] for u in units])

DM, TN = pfc7.rsa_design()
DM_ALT, _ = pfc7.rsa_design(alternative=True)
FTP = pfc7.rsa_ftest_parts(DM)
FTP_ALT = pfc7.rsa_ftest_parts(DM_ALT)
NPERM = 10000

def rsa_run(mats, dm, ftp, rng, nperm=NPERM):
    """mats: list of three conditions x units matrices (ACC, DLPFC, OFC)."""
    Y = np.column_stack([pfc7.rsa_matrix(M).ravel(order="F") for M in mats])
    C = np.eye(dm.shape[1])
    _, _, t = pfc7.ols(Y, dm, C)
    cp = pfc7.cpd(Y, dm)
    F = pfc7.rsa_fstats(Y.ravel(order="F"), ftp)
    tp = np.zeros((nperm,) + t.shape)
    Fp = np.zeros((nperm, len(F)))
    for p in range(nperm):
        pp = rng.permutation(20)
        Yp = np.column_stack([pfc7.rsa_matrix(M[pp]).ravel(order="F") for M in mats])
        tp[p] = pfc7.ols(Yp, dm, C)[2]
        Fp[p] = pfc7.rsa_fstats(Yp.ravel(order="F"), ftp)
    p1 = 1 - (t[None] > tp).mean(0)
    p2 = (np.abs(tp) >= np.abs(t)[None]).mean(0)
    pF = 1 - (F[None] > Fp).mean(0)
    pdiff = {}
    for i in range(2, 7):
        for r1 in range(3):
            for r2 in range(3):
                if r1 != r2:
                    pdiff[(i, r1, r2)] = 1 - ((t[i, r1] - t[i, r2]) > (tp[:, i, r1] - tp[:, i, r2])).mean()
    return dict(Y=Y, t=t, cpd=cp, F=F, p1=p1, p2=p2, pF=pF, pdiff=pdiff)

def rsa_table(res, names=TN):
    rows = []
    for i in range(2, 7):
        for r in range(3):
            rows.append(dict(template=names[i], area=NAMES[r + 1], T=res["t"][i, r],
                             p_one=res["p1"][i, r], p_two=res["p2"][i, r], CPD=100 * res["cpd"][i, r]))
    tb = pd.DataFrame(rows).pivot(index="template", columns="area")
    return tb

MATS = {"a": [rsa_unitmat(SEL[a]) for a in (1, 2, 3)]}
print("units entering the RSA:", {NAMES[a]: int((~np.all(m == 0, 0)).sum()) for a, m in zip((1, 2, 3), MATS["a"])})
RSA = {"a": rsa_run(MATS["a"], DM, FTP, section_rng("rsa-a"))}
print(f"RSA reading (a) with {NPERM} permutations: {time.time() - t_rsa:.0f} s")
print(rsa_table(RSA["a"]).round(4))
print("between-region F:", {TN[i]: (round(RSA["a"]["F"][i], 2), RSA["a"]["pF"][i]) for i in range(2, 7)})

A helper to judge the template claims under each reading (O8 sidedness, O9 trials).

In [21]:
IDX = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(TN)}
def sig(res, tmpl, area, side):
    return (res["p1"] if side == "one" else res["p2"])[IDX[tmpl], area - 1] < 0.05
def cpdv(res, tmpl, area):
    return res["cpd"][IDX[tmpl], area - 1]
def readings():
    for o9 in ("a", "b"):
        for o8 in ("one", "two"):
            yield o9, o8

Result: reproduced. The spatial attention template is significant in DLPFC (T = 39.90, permutation p < 0.0001), OFC (T = 4.58, p = 0.018) and ACC (T = 7.90, p = 0.0028), and its CPD is largest in DLPFC (80.2% against 13.7% in ACC and 5.1% in OFC); the between-region F is 348.5 (p < 0.0001). All four readings of O8 and O9 agree.

def judge_ofc(tmpl):
    for o9, o8 in readings():
        r = RSA[o9]
        ok = sig(r, tmpl, 3, o8) and cpdv(r, tmpl, 3) > cpdv(r, tmpl, 1) and cpdv(r, tmpl, 3) > cpdv(r, tmpl, 2)
        print(f"O9 ({o9}) O8 {o8}-sided: T OFC {r['t'][IDX[tmpl], 2]:.2f}, p "

fig4g-left-right-value¶

At cue 1, ACC and DLPFC representational similarity shows a value code modulated by whether the subject attends the left or right option.

In [25]:
def judge_lr(res_by_reading, tmpl="left/right value"):
    out = {}
    for o9, o8 in readings():
        r = res_by_reading[o9]
        ok = (sig(r, tmpl, 1, o8) and sig(r, tmpl, 2, o8) and cpdv(r, tmpl, 1) > cpdv(r, tmpl, 3)
              and cpdv(r, tmpl, 2) > cpdv(r, tmpl, 3))
        pv = (r['p1'] if o8 == 'one' else r['p2'])[IDX[tmpl]]
        print(f"O9 ({o9}) O8 {o8}-sided: T ACC/DLPFC/OFC {np.round(r['t'][IDX[tmpl]], 2)}, p {np.round(pv, 4)};"
              f" CPD % {np.round(100 * r['cpd'][IDX[tmpl]], 2)}; F p = {r['pF'][IDX[tmpl]]:.4f} -> holds: {ok}")
        out[(o9, o8)] = ok
    return out

figs4-dlpfc-top-bottom¶

Split by top and bottom cue position (40 conditions), the RSA results replicate, and DLPFC similarity is also modulated by top/bottom position, so DLPFC represents spatial position more than left/right action.

40 conditions as calculate_RSA_matrices_updown.m (conditions 1-20 with cue 1 on top, 21-40 at the bottom; within each, LP, LM, RP, RM). The measure is the criterion's: mean similarity of pairs in the same quadrant against pairs on the same side in different rows, off the diagonal.

In [28]:
side = np.r_[np.zeros(10), np.ones(10), np.zeros(10), np.ones(10)]
row = np.r_[np.zeros(20), np.ones(20)]
same_q = (side[:, None] == side[None]) & (row[:, None] == row[None]) & ~np.eye(40, dtype=bool)
same_side_diff_row = (side[:, None] == side[None]) & (row[:, None] != row[None])
S4 = {}
for a in (1, 2, 3):
    M = pfc7.rsa_matrix(rsa_unitmat(SEL[a], field="m40"))
    S4[a] = M[same_q].mean() - M[same_side_diff_row].mean()
    print(f"{NAMES[a]}: same quadrant {M[same_q].mean():.4f}, same side other row "
          f"{M[same_side_diff_row].mean():.4f}, difference {S4[a]:.4f}; matrix range "
          f"{M[~np.eye(40, dtype=bool)].min():.2f} to {M[~np.eye(40, dtype=bool)].max():.2f}")
# null for the difference: permute the 40 condition labels within each unit set
rng = section_rng("figs4")
null = {a: [] for a in (1, 2, 3)}
for a in (1, 2, 3):
    X = rsa_unitmat(SEL[a], field="m40")
    for p in range(1000):
        M = pfc7.rsa_matrix(X[rng.permutation(40)])
        null[a].append(M[same_q].mean() - M[same_side_diff_row].mean())
    print(f"{NAMES[a]}: permutation p (one-sided, 1000 label permutations, a reference not in the criterion) "
          f"{np.mean(np.array(null[a]) >= S4[a]):.3f}")
print("criterion: DLPFC difference > 0 and larger than ACC and OFC:", S4[2] > 0 and S4[2] > S4[1] and S4[2] > S4[3])

fig4-t75-latencies¶

Spatial attention reached 75% of its peak CPD at about the saccade (24, 72 and 67 ms in ACC, DLPFC, OFC); stimulus identity and attended value in OFC (269, 241 ms) and accept/reject (238 ms ACC, 224 ms OFC) followed; left/right value came later (457 ms ACC, 369 ms DLPFC).

Fig4_RSA.m computes the RSA matrix at every 1 ms from 200 ms boxcar-smoothed condition means, the CPD of each template over time, and t75 with calculate_t75max.m over the whole epoch (-199 to 600 ms). Readings of the claims file: step (a) 10 ms, (b) 1 ms; range -100 to 500 ms, with -200 to 600 ms (the script's) reported.

In [29]:
TIMEIND = np.arange(-199, 601)
def sliding_rsa_cpd(units_by_area, dm):
    Ys = []
    for units in units_by_area:
        S = np.stack([U[u]["rsa"]["s20"] for u in units], axis=1)   # 20 x units x 800
        Yt = np.zeros((400, S.shape[2]))
        for k in range(S.shape[2]):
            Yt[:, k] = pfc7.rsa_matrix(S[:, :, k]).ravel(order="F")
        Ys.append(Yt)
    Yall = np.hstack(Ys)
    c = pfc7.cpd(Yall, dm) * 100
    return Yall, c.reshape(dm.shape[1], 3, -1)   # templates x areas x time
YT, CPDT = sliding_rsa_cpd([SEL[a] for a in (1, 2, 3)], DM)
EXP75 = [("spatial attention", 1, 24), ("spatial attention", 2, 72), ("spatial attention", 3, 67),
         ("stimulus identity", 3, 269), ("attended value", 3, 241), ("accept/reject", 1, 238),
         ("accept/reject", 3, 224), ("left/right value", 1, 457), ("left/right value", 2, 369)]
TOL75 = [10, 10, 10, 26.9, 24.1, 23.8, 22.4, 45.7, 36.9]
rows = []
for step in (10, 1):
    for lo, hi in ((-100, 500), (-200, 600)):
        sel = (TIMEIND >= lo) & (TIMEIND <= hi)
        idx = np.flatnonzero(sel)[::step]
        r = dict(step=step, range=f"{lo} to {hi}")
        nwithin = 0
        for (tm, a, e), tol in zip(EXP75, TOL75):
            v, tmax, mx = pfc7.t75(CPDT[IDX[tm], a - 1, idx], TIMEIND[idx])
            r[f"{tm} {NAMES[a]}"] = v
            nwithin += abs(v - e) <= tol
        r["within tolerance"] = nwithin
        rows.append(r)
T75 = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(["step", "range"])
print(T75.T)
print("expected:", {f"{tm} {NAMES[a]}": e for tm, a, e in EXP75})
peak = {f"{tm} {NAMES[a]}": round(float(CPDT[IDX[tm], a - 1].max()), 2) for tm, a, e in EXP75}
print("peak CPD (%) of each curve:", peak)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.5))
for a in (1, 2, 3):
    for i in range(2, 7):
        ax[a - 1].plot(TIMEIND, CPDT[i, a - 1], label=TN[i])
    ax[a - 1].set_title(NAMES[a]); ax[a - 1].set_xlabel("ms after cue 1")
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7); ax[0].set_ylabel("CPD (%)")
plt.show()
print("CPD range plotted:", round(float(CPDT[2:].min()), 2), "to", round(float(CPDT[2:].max()), 2), "%")

figs5c-latency-order¶

Spatial attention is encoded significantly earlier than stimulus identity, attended value and accept/reject, and left/right value (in ACC and DLPFC) significantly later than the other variables.

Fig4_RSA.m: 100 simulations adding permuted residuals of the sliding template regression to its fitted values; the script draws one permutation of the 400 elements and applies it at every time point (reading (b)). Reading (a) draws one per time point. t75 over -199 to 600 ms at 1 ms, as the script. The variables compared in each region are those whose template is significant at 100-500 ms (one-sided permutation p < 0.05, O9 reading (a)).

In [30]:
rng = section_rng("figs5c")
Xb = DM @ np.linalg.pinv(DM) @ YT
RX = YT - Xb
sims = {"a": [], "b": []}
for rd in ("a", "b"):
    for p in range(100):
        if rd == "b":
            new = Xb + RX[rng.permutation(400)]
        else:
            perm = np.argsort(rng.random(RX.shape), axis=0)
            new = Xb + np.take_along_axis(RX, perm, axis=0)
        c = (pfc7.cpd(new, DM) * 100).reshape(7, 3, -1)
        sims[rd].append({(i, a): pfc7.t75(c[i, a - 1], TIMEIND)[0] for i in range(2, 7) for a in (1, 2, 3)})
# the script's set: the variables Fig4_RSA.m stacks for Supplementary Figure 5C (peak CPD above 10%)

              3: [IDX["attended value"], IDX["accept/reject"], IDX["stimulus identity"]]}
print("t75 point estimate (ms, 1 ms step, -199 to 600 ms) by template and area:",
      {f"{TN[i]} {NAMES[a]}": float(pfc7.t75(CPDT[i, a - 1], TIMEIND)[0]) for i in range(2, 7) for a in (1, 2, 3)})
print("significant at 100-500 ms (one-sided p < 0.05, reading (a)):",
      [f"{TN[i]} {NAMES[a]}" for i in range(2, 7) for a in (1, 2, 3) if RSA["a"]["p1"][i, a - 1] < 0.05])
print("peak CPD (%) by template and area:", {f"{TN[i]} {NAMES[a]}": round(float(CPDT[i, a - 1].max()), 1)
                                              for i in range(2, 7) for a in (1, 2, 3)})
for rd, vset in [(r_, v_) for r_ in ("a", "b") for v_ in ("significant", "script")]:
    df = pd.DataFrame(sims[rd])
    print(f"--- reading ({rd}), variables {vset}: t75 range (min to max over 100 simulations), ms")
    ok_all = True
    for a in (1, 2, 3):
        if vset == "script":
            keep_v = SCRIPT_SET[a]
        else:
            keep_v = [i for i in (2, 3, 4) if RSA["a"]["p1"][i, a - 1] < 0.05]
            if a in (1, 2) and RSA["a"]["p1"][IDX["left/right value"], a - 1] < 0.05:
                keep_v.append(IDX["left/right value"])
        rng_ = {TN[i]: (df[(i, a)].min(), df[(i, a)].max()) for i in [IDX["spatial attention"]] + keep_v}
        print(NAMES[a], {k: (float(v[0]), float(v[1])) for k, v in rng_.items()})
        sp = rng_["spatial attention"]
        others = [v for k, v in rng_.items() if k not in ("spatial attention", "left/right value")]
        early = all(sp[1] < o[0] for o in others)
        late = True
        if "left/right value" in rng_:
            lr = rng_["left/right value"]
            late = all(lr[0] > v[1] for k, v in rng_.items() if k != "left/right value")
        elif a in (1, 2):
            late = False
        print(f"   spatial attention below all others: {early}; left/right value above all others: {late}")
        ok_all &= early and late
    print(f"reading ({rd}), variables {vset}: criterion holds in every region: {ok_all}")

Result: not reproduced. The criterion asks for the spatial attention range to lie below every other kept variable and, in ACC and DLPFC, the left/right value range above every other, under one reading; no reading gives this. In OFC the attended value range reaches down to -10 ms (reading a) or -13 ms (reading b), below the top of the spatial attention range (93 or 99 ms). In ACC left/right value (252 to 492 ms, reading a; 246 to 528 ms, reading b) overlaps accept/reject (229 to 272 ms; 227 to 291 ms). Parts hold: in DLPFC, with the script's set of variables, spatial attention lies below left/right value and left/right value above it under both readings, and in ACC spatial attention lies below the other kept variables with the script's set. The test fails in at least two of the three regions under every reading, so the outcome is not reproduced; in figs1ab-cue-weights, by contrast, one component fails in one monkey and the rest holds, which is partially reproduced. The t75 point estimates of the nine claimed curves follow the paper's order. With all the significant templates, in DLPFC accept/reject (491 ms) comes after left/right value (369 ms); the other regions keep the order (ACC: spatial attention 24 ms, accept/reject 238, stimulus identity 262, left/right value 457; OFC: spatial attention 67, accept/reject 224, attended value 241, stimulus identity 269).

GLM claims (Figures 5 to 7)¶

T-statistics of the shared GLM for every unit (fitted above). Bin indices: the bin centred at 250 ms after a cue is index 35, at 300 ms index 40; response locked, the bin centred at -200 ms is index 30 (the scripts' ttR(30, ...), 1-based, is the bin centred at -210 ms; both are shown where they matter). Contrast numbers are the GLM script's (19 = EV1 + EV5, 20 = EV2 + EV6).

In [31]:
B250, B300 = int(np.flatnonzero(pfc7.TIMEBINS == 250)[0]), int(np.flatnonzero(pfc7.TIMEBINS == 300)[0])
def tst(units, ep, con, b, kind="t"):
    """T-statistic (or `kind`='b' the contrast estimate) of contrast number `con` at bin `b`."""
    return np.array([G[u][kind + ep][con - 1, b] for u in units])
def tmean(units, ep, evs, b):
    """Reading (a): the mean of the EVs' T-statistics."""
    return np.mean([tst(units, ep, e, b) for e in evs], axis=0)
def pear(x, y):
    ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    r, p = stats.pearsonr(x[ok], y[ok])
    return r, p, int(ok.sum())

    ra = pear(tmean(units, "X1", [1, 5], B250), tmean(units, "X2", [2, 6], B250))

    return ra, rb

fig5gj-cross-correlation-dynamics¶

Cross-correlating the OFC value subspaces across time shows the same population subspace shifting its value encoding from positive to negative as the subject saccades around the screen.

Fig5_OFCcrosscorrelation.m and cross_corr_tstats.m: for each of four EV pairs (EV6/EV5, EV2/EV1, EV3/EV1, EV3/EV2) the correlation across OFC neurons of the T-statistics at every pair of bins, for every pair of cue epochs (rows: the first EV's epoch). The script computes each pair of epochs as its own 61 x 61 map, with its own null: clusters of |r| > 0.2, 8-connected (bwconncomp), significant when larger than the 99.9th percentile of the largest cluster in 1000 permutations of the neurons of the second EV. All nine blocks of each map are computed. As a variant, each map is also computed as one 183 x 183 map over the three epochs with a single null, the reading of the criterion's "every pair of time points over the cue 1, 2 and 3 epochs" that the verifier raised.

In [37]:
rng = section_rng("fig5gj")
EPS = ("X1", "X2", "X3")
def tmat(units, ep, ev):
    return np.stack([G[u]["t" + ep][ev - 1] for u in units])   # neurons x bins
def ccmat(A, B):
    A = (A - A.mean(0)) / A.std(0); B = (B - B.mean(0)) / B.std(0)
    return A.T @ B / A.shape[0]
def cluster_test(A, B, thr=0.2, nperm=1000):
    """cross_corr_tstats.m: map, clusters of |r| > thr (8-connected, as bwconncomp), and the
    99.9th percentile of the largest cluster over `nperm` permutations of B's neurons."""
    cm = ccmat(A, B)
    lab, n = pfc7.clusters(np.abs(cm) > thr)
    sizes = np.bincount(lab.ravel())[1:]
    null = np.zeros(nperm)
    for p in range(nperm):
        cp = ccmat(A, B[rng.permutation(B.shape[0])])
        l2, n2 = pfc7.clusters(np.abs(cp) > thr)
        null[p] = np.bincount(l2.ravel())[1:].max() if n2 else 0
    crit = np.percentile(null, 99.9)
    return cm, lab, sizes, crit
def at_point(res, i, j):
    """Size of the cluster through bin (i, j), whether it passes, and r there."""
    cm, lab, sizes, crit = res
    l = lab[i, j]
    return (int(sizes[l - 1]) if l else 0), bool(l and sizes[l - 1] > crit), float(cm[i, j])
units = SEL5[3]
PAIRS = [(6, 5, "X2", "X2"), (2, 1, "X3", "X3"), (3, 1, "X3", "X3"), (3, 2, "X3", "X3")]
SIGN = {(6, 5): -1, (2, 1): 1, (3, 1): -1, (3, 2): -1}
# Fig5_OFCcrosscorrelation.m: each pair of cue epochs is its own 61 x 61 map with its own null
BLOCKS = {}
rows = []
for e1, e2, _, _ in PAIRS:
    for ep1 in EPS:
        for ep2 in EPS:
            res = cluster_test(tmat(units, ep1, e1), tmat(units, ep2, e2))
            BLOCKS[(e1, e2, ep1, ep2)] = res
            cm, lab, sizes, crit = res
            sgn = np.array([np.sign(cm[lab == k + 1].mean()) for k in range(len(sizes))])
            big = sizes > crit
            rows.append(dict(map=f"EV{e1} x EV{e2}", rows=ep1, cols=ep2, threshold=round(crit),
                             n_sig_clusters=int(big.sum()), largest_pos=int(sizes[big & (sgn > 0)].max(initial=0)),
                             largest_neg=int(sizes[big & (sgn < 0)].max(initial=0)),
                             r_250=round(float(cm[B250, B250]), 3)))
print("every block of the four maps (clusters larger than the block's 99.9th percentile):")
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))
GJ = {}
for e1, e2, ep1, ep2 in PAIRS:
    size, sig_, r = at_point(BLOCKS[(e1, e2, ep1, ep2)], B250, B250)
    GJ[(e1, e2)] = sig_ and np.sign(r) == SIGN[(e1, e2)]
    print(f"EV{e1} ({ep1}) x EV{e2} ({ep2}): r at (250, 250) = {r:.3f}; cluster there of {size} bins, threshold "
          f"{BLOCKS[(e1, e2, ep1, ep2)][3]:.0f}; significant with the expected sign: {GJ[(e1, e2)]}")
size, sig_, r = at_point(BLOCKS[(6, 5, "X2", "X1")], B250, B250)
pos_early = sig_ and r > 0
print(f"EV6 (cue 2) x EV5 (cue 1): r at (250, 250) = {r:.3f}; cluster {size} bins, "
      f"threshold {BLOCKS[(6, 5, 'X2', 'X1')][3]:.0f}; significant positive: {pos_early}")
print("criterion holds (separate blocks, as the script):", all(GJ.values()) and pos_early)
# Variant: one 183 x 183 map over the three epochs (cue 1, 2, 3 bins concatenated), one null
nb = len(pfc7.TIMEBINS)
off = {ep: k * nb for k, ep in enumerate(EPS)}
FULL = {}
for e1, e2, _, _ in PAIRS:
    FULL[(e1, e2)] = cluster_test(np.hstack([tmat(units, ep, e1) for ep in EPS]),
                                  np.hstack([tmat(units, ep, e2) for ep in EPS]))
ok_full = []
for e1, e2, ep1, ep2 in PAIRS:
    size, sig_, r = at_point(FULL[(e1, e2)], off[ep1] + B250, off[ep2] + B250)
    ok_full.append(sig_ and np.sign(r) == SIGN[(e1, e2)])
    print(f"183 x 183 map EV{e1} x EV{e2}: cluster through ({ep1} 250, {ep2} 250) {size} bins, threshold "
          f"{FULL[(e1, e2)][3]:.0f}, expected sign and significant: {ok_full[-1]}")
size, sig_, r = at_point(FULL[(6, 5)], off["X2"] + B250, off["X1"] + B250)
ok_full.append(sig_ and r > 0)
print(f"183 x 183 map EV6 x EV5: cluster through (X2 250, X1 250) {size} bins, r = {r:.3f}, significant positive: {ok_full[-1]}")
print("criterion holds (one map over the three epochs):", all(ok_full))
# The two cue 3 option maps pass the single-map variant by narrow margins: their thresholds with
# 10 other seeds (1000 permutations each) and with 10000 permutations
for e1, e2 in ((3, 1), (3, 2)):
    A_ = np.hstack([tmat(units, ep, e1) for ep in EPS]); B_ = np.hstack([tmat(units, ep, e2) for ep in EPS])
    size = at_point(FULL[(e1, e2)], off["X3"] + B250, off["X3"] + B250)[0]
    crits = []
    for sd in range(10):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
        crits.append(cluster_test(A_, B_)[3])

Result: reproduced. With each pair of epochs as its own 61 x 61 map and null, as the script computes them, each of the four maps has a cluster through the 250 ms point of its cue of the expected sign and larger than the 99.9th percentile of 1000 permutations (884, 1839, 1105 and 817 bins against thresholds of 442 to 487), and EV 6 at cue 2 with EV 5 at cue 1 forms a positive cluster (r = 0.755 at 250, 250 ms; 1622 bins against 640). With one 183 x 183 map over the three epochs and a single null, the criterion also holds, with narrow margins for the two cue 3 option maps (EV 3 with EV 1, 1105 bins against 1083; EV 3 with EV 2, 817 against 810). That variant depends on the seed: with 10 other seeds the EV 3 with EV 2 cluster passes in 0 of 10 (thresholds 853 to 1262) and fails with 10000 permutations (threshold 990); EV 3 with EV 1 passes in 7 of 10 and with 10000 permutations (984). So the single-map reading does not hold, and the outcome rests on the script's separate maps, which pass by wide margins.

fig6a-acc-belief-subspace¶

In ACC the T-statistics of the four belief confirmation regressors (cues 2 and 3, option and attribute trials) correlate positively with each other and with cue 1 value, a stable belief confirmation code not present in OFC or DLPFC.

Fig6_ACCmultiplesignals_R3_version.m: contrast 19 at cue 1 and EVs 13 and 14 at cue 2, 15 and 16 at cue 3, all at 300 ms, correlated across neurons in each region (units: SEL, the script's selection). Readings of the claims file: (a) T-statistics, (b) OLS coefficients; cue 1 value as the mean of the EV1 and EV5 T-statistics or as contrast 19.

LAB6 = ["cue1 value", "EV13", "EV14", "EV15", "EV16"]
iu5 = np.triu_indices(5, 1)
def belief_mat(units, kind, cue1):
    if kind == "t" and cue1 == "mean":
        c1 = tmean(units, "X1", [1, 5], B300)
    else:
        c1 = tst(units, "X1", 19, B300, kind)
    return np.column_stack([c1, tst(units, "X2", 13, B300, kind), tst(units, "X2", 14, B300, kind),
                            tst(units, "X3", 15, B300, kind), tst(units, "X3", 16, B300, kind)])
R6 = {}
for kind in ("t", "b"):
    for cue1 in ("contrast", "mean"):
        if kind == "b" and cue1 == "mean":
            continue
        for a in (1, 2, 3):
            M = belief_mat(SEL[a], kind, cue1)
            M = M[np.isfinite(M).all(1)]
            r = np.corrcoef(M.T)
            p = np.ones_like(r)
            for i in range(5):
                for j in range(5):
                    if i != j:
                        p[i, j] = stats.pearsonr(M[:, i], M[:, j])[1]
            iu = np.triu_indices(5, 1)
            R6[(kind, cue1, a)] = dict(r=r, p=p, n=len(M))
            npos = int(((r[iu] > 0) & (p[iu] < 0.05)).sum())
            print(f"{'T-statistics' if kind == 't' else 'coefficients'}, cue 1 as {cue1}, {NAMES[a]} (n = {len(M)}):"
                  f" r = {np.round(r[iu], 3)}, positive with p < 0.05: {npos} of 10")
    print()

Projections onto the ACC subspaces (fig6c, fig6d, fig6e)¶

Fig6_ACCmultiplesignals_R3_version.m and InfoGathering_Neurons_Ramp_to_choice.m. Weights per ACC unit from the GLM on one half of trials: belief confirmation, the mean of the T-statistics of EVs 13 to 16 at 300 ms after their cues; action, the mean of EVs 17 and 18 at the response bin the scripts index as 30 (centred 210 ms before the response); the scripts' design is [demeaned belief, demeaned action, constant, mean of EVs 11 and 12 at that bin], and the projected data are each unit's mean firing in five reaction-time bins (all trials of the other half, including those with 2 cues), z-scored by the session mean and SD, 200 ms boxcar every 10 ms; baseline the projection at cue 1 onset +/- 50 ms of the same bin (and choice). The scripts' RT bins are fixed: below 1200, 1200-1400, 1400-1600, 1600-1800 and from 1800 ms after cue 1 onset. The claims file's readings: O4 (a) odd/even, (b) 100 random halves, here the halves the scripts drew and stored (drawn per unit), and (c) 100 random halves drawn once per session and shared by its units; O5 (a) quintiles per session, (b) quintiles per monkey, and the scripts' fixed bins; O6 (a) Hz, (b) z-scored; O7 (a) mean of T-statistics, (b) T-statistic of the mean coefficient.

Every combination is also run with the projection of the Methods (Projection of ACC activity: "we then regressed this matrix onto a projection matrix composed of two key 'weights' per neuron", "This projection matrix therefore had dimensions neurons*(2 PEs)"), the design [belief, action] with no constant, and with the action weights at the bin centred 200 ms before the response ("EV 17 and EV 18, 200ms prior to response onset"). The tables below are for the scripts' design and bin; a summary follows each for the four combinations of design and bin.

In [43]:
acc = SEL[1]
RBS = {-210: 29, -200: 30}   # response bins for the action weights: the scripts' index 30 (1-based), centred -210 ms; and -200 ms (Methods)
def weights_from(tg, kind, rb):
    """tg: dict of epoch -> (cope, t) arrays (contrasts x bins) from one half."""
    def comb(items):
        if kind == "a":
            return np.mean([tg[ep][1][ev - 1, b] for ep, ev, b in items])
        cs = np.array([tg[ep][0][ev - 1, b] for ep, ev, b in items])
        vs = np.array([(tg[ep][0][ev - 1, b] / tg[ep][1][ev - 1, b]) ** 2 for ep, ev, b in items])
        return cs.mean() / np.sqrt(vs.mean() / len(items))
    bel = comb([("X3", 15, B300), ("X3", 16, B300), ("X2", 14, B300), ("X2", 13, B300)])
    lr = comb([("XR", 17, rb), ("XR", 18, rb)])
    o, a_ = tg["XR"][1][10, rb], tg["XR"][1][11, rb]
    return np.array([bel, lr, o, a_])
def half_fit(d, k):
    """GLM on the trials of `k` (all with 3 or more cues), at the bins the weights use only."""
    X = pfc7.glm_design(d)
    P = np.linalg.pinv(X[k])
    dof = k.sum() - np.linalg.matrix_rank(X[k])
    pre = np.diag(P @ P.T)
    out = {}
    for ep, bins in (("X2", [B300]), ("X3", [B300]), ("XR", list(RBS.values()))):
        cope = np.full((18, 61), np.nan); t = np.full((18, 61), np.nan)
        for b in bins:
            y = d[ep][k][:, b].astype(float)
            pe = P @ y
            sig2 = ((y - X[k] @ pe) ** 2).sum() / dof
            cope[:, b] = pe
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
                t[:, b] = pe / np.sqrt(pre * sig2)
        out[ep] = (cope, t)
    return out
# RT bins
rt_all = {u: U[u]["Response_time"] - U[u]["Cue1_ON"] for u in acc}
sess_rt = {}
for u in acc:
    sess_rt.setdefault((U[u]["sb"], U[u]["snum"]), rt_all[u])
mon_rt = {sb: np.concatenate([v for (s_, _), v in sess_rt.items() if s_ == sb]) for sb in ("M", "F")}
def rt_labels(u, rd):
    rt = rt_all[u]
    if rd == "script":
        edges = [1200, 1400, 1600, 1800]
    elif rd == "a":
        edges = np.quantile(sess_rt[(U[u]["sb"], U[u]["snum"])], [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8])
    else:
        edges = np.quantile(mon_rt[U[u]["sb"]], [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8])
    return np.searchsorted(edges, rt, side="right")
O5S = ("script", "a", "b")
LAB = {rd: {u: rt_labels(u, rd) for u in acc} for rd in O5S}
print("trials per RT bin, pooled over ACC units:",
      {rd: np.bincount(np.concatenate(list(v.values())), minlength=5).tolist() for rd, v in LAB.items()})
def averages(u, mask, labels):
    """Mean z-scored activity per RT bin: cue locked (c5), and per bin and choice, cue and response
    locked (c10, r10: left, right), and the choice-signed mean (csg, rsg; right trials times -1).
    Also the mean sign per bin (for converting the signed mean to Hz)."""
    d = U[u]
    left = d["Left_choice"] == 1
    sgn = np.where(left, 1.0, -1.0)
    W5 = np.full((len(mask), 5), 0.0); W10 = np.zeros((len(mask), 10)); Wsg = np.zeros((len(mask), 5))
    msg = np.full(5, np.nan)
    for k in range(5):
        s_ = mask & (labels == k)
        if s_.any():
            W5[s_, k] = 1 / s_.sum(); Wsg[s_, k] = sgn[s_] / s_.sum(); msg[k] = sgn[s_].mean()
        else:
            W5[:, k] = np.nan; Wsg[:, k] = np.nan
        for c, cs in enumerate((left, ~left)):
            s2 = s_ & cs
            if s2.any():
                W10[s2, 2 * k + c] = 1 / s2.sum()
            else:
                W10[:, 2 * k + c] = np.nan
    L1, LR = d["L1"], d["LR"]
    return dict(c5=W5.T @ L1, c10=W10.T @ L1, r10=W10.T @ LR, csg=Wsg.T @ L1, rsg=Wsg.T @ LR, msg=msg)
def to_hz(A, u):
    d = U[u]
    out = {k: A[k] * d["sdev"] + d["men"] for k in ("c5", "c10", "r10")}
    for k in ("csg", "rsg"):
        out[k] = A[k] * d["sdev"] + d["men"] * A["msg"][:, None]
    return out
def project(W, D, design="script"):
    """OLS of the neurons x columns data on the design built from the neurons x 4 weights:
    "script", Fig6_ACCmultiplesignals_R3_version.m, [demeaned belief, demeaned action, constant,
    mean of EVs 11 and 12]; "methods", the neurons x 2 matrix of the Methods (Projection of ACC
    activity: "a projection matrix composed of two key 'weights' per neuron"), [belief, action]."""
    ok = np.isfinite(D).all(1) & np.isfinite(W).all(1)
    if design == "methods":
        cols = [W[ok, 0], W[ok, 1]]
    else:
        cols = [W[ok, 0] - W[ok, 0].mean(), W[ok, 1] - W[ok, 1].mean(), np.ones(ok.sum()),
                (W[ok, 2] + W[ok, 3]) / 2]
    return np.linalg.pinv(np.column_stack(cols)) @ D[ok], int(ok.sum())
CUE_T, RESP_T = pfc7.CUE1_LONG, pfc7.RESP_LONG
BASE_W = (CUE_T >= -50) & (CUE_T <= 50)
KEYS = ("c5", "c10", "r10", "csg", "rsg")
VARS6 = [("script", -210), ("script", -200), ("methods", -210), ("methods", -200)]
def proj_one(tg, avs, o7, design, rbt):
    W = np.array([weights_from(tg[u], o7, RBS[rbt]) for u in acc])
    out, ns = {}, []
    for k in KEYS:
        coef, n = project(W, avs[k], design)
        out[k] = coef.reshape(coef.shape[0], avs["shape"][k], -1)
        ns.append(n)
    return out, ns

for wh, dh in (("odd", "even"), ("even", "odd")):
    tg_oe.append({u: {ep: (G[u][f"b{ep}_{wh}"], G[u][f"t{ep}_{wh}"]) for ep in ("X2", "X3", "XR")} for u in acc})
    dm_oe.append({u: (G[u]["odd"] if dh == "odd" else ~G[u]["odd"]) for u in acc})
SPLITS["a"] = (tg_oe, dm_oe)
# O4 (b): the 100 random halves the scripts drew and stored (randproj_trials of
# info_gathering_cue123_alltrials_attentional_final.mat, drawn per unit over its trials with 3 or
# more cues); weights from one half, data from all other trials (InfoGathering_Neurons_Ramp_to_choice.m)
def split_fits(draws):
    tgs, dms = [], []
    for s_ in range(100):
        tg, dmk = {}, {}
        for u in acc:
            d = U[u]
            k3 = np.flatnonzero(d["num_pics_viewed"] >= 3)
            k = np.zeros(len(d["condition"]), bool)
            k[k3[draws[u][:, s_]]] = True
            tg[u] = half_fit(d, k)
            dmk[u] = ~k
        tgs.append(tg); dms.append(dmk)
    return tgs, dms

# O4 (c): 100 random halves drawn once per session and shared by its units, so that no trial of a
# unit's weights is a projected trial of a simultaneously recorded unit (verifier, round 1, point 6)
rng = section_rng("fig6-projection")
n3 = {}

PROJV, NKEEP, SPLIT6C = {v: {} for v in VARS6}, set(), {}
W6C = {"a": (100, 500), "b": (0, 500)}
for o4, (tgl, dml) in SPLITS.items():
    for o5 in O5S:
        acc_ = {}
        for s_ in range(len(dml)):
            avz = {u: averages(u, dml[s_][u], LAB[o5][u]) for u in acc}
            avh = {u: to_hz(avz[u], u) for u in acc}
            for o6, av in (("a", avh), ("b", avz)):
                avs = {k: np.stack([av[u][k].ravel() for u in acc]) for k in KEYS}
                avs["shape"] = {k: av[acc[0]][k].shape[0] for k in KEYS}
                for o7 in ("a", "b"):
                    for var in VARS6:
                        pr, ns = proj_one(tgl[s_], avs, o7, *var)
                        NKEEP.update(ns)
                        cb = pr["c5"][0] - pr["c5"][0][:, BASE_W].mean(1, keepdims=True)
                        for wn, (lo, hi) in W6C.items():
                            w = (CUE_T >= lo) & (CUE_T <= hi)
                            SPLIT6C.setdefault((var, o4, o5, o6, o7, wn), []).append(bool(cb[0, w].mean() > cb[4, w].mean()))
                        for k, v in pr.items():
                            acc_.setdefault((var, o6, o7, k), []).append(v)
        for (var, o6, o7, k), v in acc_.items():
            PROJV[var].setdefault((o4, o5, o6, o7), {})[k] = np.mean(v, axis=0)
        del acc_

      f"neurons kept per projection {min(NKEEP)} to {max(NKEEP)} of {len(acc)}")

def bl(P, comp, key):
    """Baseline-corrected projection of component `comp` (0 belief, 1 action) for data `key`."""
    base_key = {"c5": "c5", "c10": "c10", "r10": "c10", "csg": "csg", "rsg": "csg"}[key]
    b0 = P[base_key][comp][:, BASE_W].mean(1, keepdims=True)
    return P[key][comp] - b0

# bin with one trial; those traces are compared with the time average of the trial here

for s_ in range(NS6):

        for kind, here, stored, sel in (

                ("r", av["r10"], ST_R[u - 1, :, :, :, s_].transpose(1, 2, 0).reshape(10, -1),
                 [mask & (lab == k) & cs for k in range(5) for cs in (left, ~left)])):
            for j, m in enumerate(sel):

                    one[kind][0] += 1
                    one[kind][1] += bool(np.allclose(stored[j], here[j].mean(), atol=1e-5))
                elif m.sum() > 1:

def f6c_table(PR, var):
    rows = []
    for key, P in PR.items():
        c = bl(P, 0, "c5")
        r = dict(zip(("O4", "O5", "O6", "O7"), key))
        for wn, (lo, hi) in W6C.items():
            w = (CUE_T >= lo) & (CUE_T <= hi)
            r[f"short-long {lo}-{hi}"] = c[0, w].mean() - c[4, w].mean()
            if key[0] != "a":
                r[f"splits {lo}-{hi}"] = int(np.sum(SPLIT6C[(var,) + key + (wn,)]))
        w2 = (CUE_T >= 500) & (CUE_T <= 1000)
        r["short-long 500-1000"] = c[0, w2].mean() - c[4, w2].mean()
        rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(["O4", "O5", "O6", "O7"])

Result: reproduced. In all 36 combinations of readings the belief projection is higher for the shortest than for the longest RT bin over 100-500 ms and 0-500 ms after cue 1 (for example a difference of 0.445 with odd/even halves, the scripts' bins and rates in Hz), and with 100 random halves in 98 to 100 of the splits. The same holds in all 36 with the Methods' two-column projection and with the action weights at -200 ms (smallest difference 0.012). The data projected here equal those the scripts stored for their first five random halves to within 1.4e-07 (every ACC unit, cue and response locked), apart from bins with a single trial, which the script stores as that trial's average over time (a quirk of MATLAB's mean on one row).

fig6d-belief-ramp-to-choice¶

Irrespective of reaction time, ACC activity in the belief confirmation subspace ramps up shortly before the joystick movement.

The scripts' response-locked belief trace averages the left- and right-choice projections; the criterion compares the mean over -200 to 0 ms with that over -500 to -300 ms in each RT bin.

late = (RESP_T >= -200) & (RESP_T <= 0)
early = (RESP_T >= -500) & (RESP_T <= -300)
def f6d_table(PR):
    rows = []
    for key, P in PR.items():
        r10 = bl(P, 0, "r10")
        tr = np.stack([r10[0::2], r10[1::2]]).mean(0)
        rise = tr[:, late].mean(1) - tr[:, early].mean(1)
        rows.append(dict(zip(("O4", "O5", "O6", "O7"), key), **{f"bin{k + 1}": rise[k] for k in range(5)},
                         n_rising=int((rise > 0).sum())))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(["O4", "O5", "O6", "O7"])

fig6e-action-subspace-ramp¶

ACC activity in the left/right action selection subspace ramps up as evidence is revealed and peaks immediately before the response.

win = (RESP_T >= -500) & (RESP_T <= 100)
def f6e_table(PR):
    rows = []
    for key, P in PR.items():
        r10 = bl(P, 1, "r10")
        for sgn_rd, tr in (("a", r10[0::2] - r10[1::2]), ("b", bl(P, 1, "rsg"))):
            rise = tr[:, late].mean(1) - tr[:, early].mean(1)
            tpk = RESP_T[win][np.argmax(tr[:, win], axis=1)]
            ok = (rise > 0) & (tpk >= -200) & (tpk <= 100)
            rows.append(dict(zip(("O4", "O5", "O6", "O7"), key), sign=sgn_rd,
                             **{f"rise{k + 1}": rise[k] for k in range(5)},
                             **{f"peak{k + 1}": int(tpk[k]) for k in range(5)}, n_ok=int(ok.sum())))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(["O4", "O5", "O6", "O7", "sign"])
f6e = f6e_table(PROJ)
print(f6e.round(3).to_string())
print("readings where every bin rises and peaks between -200 and 100 ms:", int((f6e.n_ok == 5).sum()), "of", len(f6e))

Result: reproduced, under 12 of 72 readings. The action projection rises before the response in every RT bin under all 72 readings and all four combinations of design and bin. With the scripts' design and bin its peak falls between -200 and 100 ms in all five bins under 12 of 72 readings, among them the scripts' own (their stored halves, their RT bins, z-scored rates, mean T-statistics, left minus right). With the action weights at -200 ms 16 of 72 hold, with the Methods' two-column projection 6 of 72 at either bin. In the other readings one or two bins peak 10 to 60 ms before -200 ms (for example -240 ms in the longest bin, -260 ms in the fourth bin with quintiles per monkey and z-scored rates).

fig7a-ofc-value-difference-neurons¶

At all three time points (cue 2 against cue 1, cue 3 against cue 1, cue 3 against cue 2), a greater proportion of single neurons encoded value difference between attended and unattended cues in OFC than in ACC and DLPFC.

Units SEL5 (Fig7_single_neurons_cue2and3.m). The significance level has three readings in the claims file, as amended after a reader's answer (questions/hunt-2018.yaml): p < 0.05 (|T| > 1.96), p < 0.01 (|T| > 2.576), and (c) |T| > 1.64 on each of the three tests, the script's threshold (its comment reads norminv(0.05)). The claim holds when OFC leads at all three tests under one reading of the bin, the trial types and the level.

In [48]:
TESTS = {"a": [("X2", 6, 5, 31), ("X3", 3, 1, 32), ("X3", 3, 2, 33)],
         "b": [("X2", 6, 5, 31), ("X3", (7, 9), 5, (36, 38)), ("X3", (7, 9), 6, (37, 39))]}
def passes(units, test, b, thr):
    ep, att, un, dif = test
    out = np.zeros(len(units), bool)
    atts = att if isinstance(att, tuple) else (att,)
    difs = dif if isinstance(dif, tuple) else (dif,)
    for at, df in zip(atts, difs):
        ta, tu, td = tst(units, ep, at, b), tst(units, ep, un, b), tst(units, ep, df, b)
        out |= (np.abs(ta) > thr) & (np.abs(tu) > thr) & (np.abs(td) > thr) & (np.sign(ta) != np.sign(tu))
    return out
F7 = {}
for tt in ("a", "b"):
    for o3, b in (("250", B250), ("300", B300)):
        for o2, thr in (("0.05", 1.96), ("0.01", 2.576), ("script 1.64", 1.64)):
            fr = {}
            anyp = {}
            for a in (1, 2, 3):
                ps = [passes(SEL5[a], t, b, thr) for t in TESTS[tt]]
                fr[a] = [100 * p.mean() for p in ps]
                anyp[a] = 100 * np.any(ps, axis=0).mean()
            ofc_top = all(fr[3][i] > fr[1][i] and fr[3][i] > fr[2][i] for i in range(3))
            F7[(tt, o3, o2)] = dict(fr=fr, any=anyp, ofc_top=ofc_top,
                                    any_top=anyp[3] > anyp[1] and anyp[3] > anyp[2])
            chis = [pfc7.chi2_yates(round(fr[3][i] * len(SEL5[3]) / 100), len(SEL5[3]),
                                    round(fr[x][i] * len(SEL5[x]) / 100), len(SEL5[x]))[1] for i in range(3) for x in (1, 2)]
            print(f"trial types ({tt}), bin {o3} ms, threshold {o2}: % ACC {np.round(fr[1], 1)}, DLPFC "
                  f"{np.round(fr[2], 1)}, OFC {np.round(fr[3], 1)}; OFC highest at all three: {ofc_top};"
                  f" chi2 p OFC vs ACC/DLPFC {[float('%.2g' % c) for c in chis]}")
# time course with the script's threshold, any bin: the script plots the percentage per bin
for a in (1, 2, 3):
    ps = np.mean([[passes(SEL5[a], t, b, 1.64) for b in range(61)] for t in TESTS["a"]], axis=2)
    print(f"{NAMES[a]}: % passing per bin (script threshold), max over bins of each test: {np.round(ps.max(1) * 100, 1)}")

        fr = {a: [100 * passes([u for u in SEL5[a] if info.loc[u, "subject"] == sb], t, b, 1.96).mean()
                  for t in TESTS["a"]] for a in (1, 2, 3)}
        print(f"monkey {sb}, trial types (a), bin {o3}, p < 0.05: % ACC {np.round(fr[1], 1)}, DLPFC {np.round(fr[2], 1)},"
              f" OFC {np.round(fr[3], 1)}")

Result: reproduced. With the Figure 5 trial types (reading a), OFC has the largest proportion at all three tests at 250 ms and p < 0.05 (OFC 6.0, 4.4, 6.6% against ACC 5.3, 3.2, 4.8% and DLPFC 1.5, 2.2, 2.2%), at 300 ms and p < 0.01 (OFC 1.6, 1.6, 3.3% against ACC 1.1, 0.5, 1.1% and DLPFC 1.5, 1.5, 1.5%), and with the script's threshold at both bins (250 ms: OFC 8.2, 7.7, 11.0% against ACC 6.3, 4.8, 7.4% and DLPFC 6.0, 3.0, 3.0%). It fails at 250 ms with p < 0.01 and at 300 ms with p < 0.05, and under the attribute-trial reading (b) in every combination. The differences are small: at 250 ms and p < 0.05 none of the six pairwise chi-square tests is below 0.05 (smallest p = 0.084), and by monkey OFC leads at all three tests in M (6.2, 6.2, 8.6%) but not in F, where ACC is higher at both cue 3 tests (3.2 and 7.4% against OFC 3.0 and 5.0%).

Cue 1 single-neuron regression (claims fig8-*)¶

The claims file's readings: regressors (a) value (rank -2 to 2), value x side (left 1, right -1), value x attribute (probability 1, magnitude -1), value x row (top 1, bottom -1), the three main effects and a constant; (b) the four value regressors and a constant. Windows (i) 100-500 ms (the mean of the bins centred at 200 and 400 ms, which tile 101-500 ms), (ii) the bin at 250 ms, (iii) at 300 ms. Trials O9 (a) all, (b) 3 or more cues. Significance O2 (a) p < 0.05, (b) p < 0.01, two-sided on the coefficient. The binomial test is the script's, 2 x P(X > k) at a chance rate equal to the significance level; the chi-square is chi2.m (Yates). Units SEL (Fig8 script).

The script's own regression (InfoGathering_Neurons_Cue1_regression.m: 13 regressors on raw values, significance from 1000 permutations corrected over the bins from 0 to 500 ms) is run as a further variant.

In [53]:
B200, B400 = int(np.flatnonzero(pfc7.TIMEBINS == 200)[0]), int(np.flatnonzero(pfc7.TIMEBINS == 400)[0])
def cue1_X(d, rd):
    v = d["Lreg"][:, 0] + d["Rreg"][:, 0] - 3
    s_ = np.where(d["Lreg"][:, 0] > 0, 1.0, -1.0)
    a_ = np.where(d["P_first"] > 0, 1.0, -1.0)
    r_ = np.where(np.isin(d["First_pos"], (1, 3)), 1.0, -1.0)
    cols = [v, v * s_, v * a_, v * r_]
    if rd == "a":
        cols += [s_, a_, r_]
    return np.column_stack(cols + [np.ones(len(v))])
def cue1_y(d, win):
    X1 = d["X1"].astype(float) * 1000
    return {"i": (X1[:, B200] + X1[:, B400]) / 2, "ii": X1[:, B250], "iii": X1[:, B300]}[win]
F8 = {}
for rd in ("a", "b"):
    for win in ("i", "ii", "iii"):
        for o9 in ("a", "b"):
            P_ = {}
            for a in (1, 2, 3):
                ps = []
                for u in SEL[a]:
                    d = U[u]
                    k = np.ones(len(d["condition"]), bool) if o9 == "a" else d["num_pics_viewed"] >= 3
                    X = cue1_X(d, rd)[k]
                    y = cue1_y(d, win)[k]
                    _, _, t = pfc7.ols(y[:, None], X, np.eye(X.shape[1])[:4])
                    dof = X.shape[0] - np.linalg.matrix_rank(X)
                    ps.append(2 * stats.t.sf(np.abs(t[:, 0]), dof))
                P_[a] = np.array(ps)   # units x 4 (value, action, attribute, spatial)
            F8[(rd, win, o9)] = P_
VAR8 = ["value", "action value", "attribute value", "spatial value"]
def f8_counts(key, alpha):
    P_ = F8[key]
    return {a: (P_[a] < alpha).sum(0) for a in (1, 2, 3)}, {a: len(P_[a]) for a in (1, 2, 3)}

           for u in SEL[a]]
    SIG8[a] = np.array([r_[0] for r_ in res]); T8[a] = [r_[1] for r_ in res]
print(f"script regression with permutations: {time.time() - t8:.0f} s")

def f8_all():
    """(key, alpha, counts k[a][var], n[a]) for every reading, then the script's with its flags
    computed here and with the flags the authors stored (SIG8_STORED, next cell)."""
    for key in F8:
        for alpha in (0.05, 0.01):
            k_, n_ = f8_counts(key, alpha)
            yield key + (str(alpha),), alpha, k_, n_
    yield ("script",), 0.05, {a: SIG8[a].sum(0) for a in (1, 2, 3)}, {a: len(SIG8[a]) for a in (1, 2, 3)}
    yield ("script", "stored flags"), 0.05, {a: SIG8_STORED[a].sum(0) for a in (1, 2, 3)}, {a: len(SIG8_STORED[a]) for a in (1, 2, 3)}

The script's regression is checked against the results the authors stored in the data set (neuronal_regression_results/info_gathering_cue1_both.mat, written by InfoGathering_Neurons_Cue1_regression.m): its T-statistics of contrasts 26, 41, 51 and 42 for each unit, and its significant_neuron flags, from which Fig8_single_neuron_coding.m computes the fractions and binomial tests. The stored flags come from the authors' own permutations, so they agree with the flags here up to permutation noise; the fractions they give are shown as the paper's own.

holds under 26 of 26 readings (the last two are the script's, flags here and flags stored); with the exact binomial test under 26

Result: reproduced. Under all 24 readings and the script's own regression, the fraction encoding cue 1 value is above chance with binomial p < 1e-7 in every region (script: ACC 54.0%, DLPFC 41.8%, OFC 59.0%), also with the exact binomial test. The script's regression gives the T-statistics the authors stored to within 3.3e-07, and the authors' stored flags give 54.5%, 41.0% and 56.8%.

fig8-action-value-acc-dlpfc¶

About 18% of ACC and DLPFC neurons encoded left/right action value at cue 1, above chance and more than OFC, which encoded action value at chance level.

In [56]:
nok = nok_x = nrd = 0
for key, alpha, k_, n_ in f8_all():
    fr = {a: 100 * k_[a][1] / n_[a] for a in (1, 2, 3)}
    pb = {a: pfc7.binom_p_code(k_[a][1], n_[a], alpha) for a in (1, 2, 3)}
    px = {a: pfc7.binom_p_exact(k_[a][1], n_[a], alpha) for a in (1, 2, 3)}
    pc = {a: pfc7.chi2_yates(k_[a][1], n_[a], k_[3][1], n_[3])[1] for a in (1, 2)}
    above = all(fr[a] > fr[3] and pc[a] < 0.05 for a in (1, 2))
    tests = all(pb[a] < 1e-5 for a in (1, 2)) and above and pb[3] >= 0.05
    tests_x = all(px[a] < 1e-5 for a in (1, 2)) and above and px[3] >= 0.05
    within = all(abs(fr[a] - 18) <= 1.8 for a in (1, 2))
    nrd += 1; nok += tests and within; nok_x += tests_x and within
    print(key, f"ACC {fr[1]:.1f}% (binom p={pb[1]:.1g}, exact {px[1]:.1g}, chi2 vs OFC p={pc[1]:.2g}), DLPFC {fr[2]:.1f}% "
          f"(p={pb[2]:.1g}, exact {px[2]:.1g}, chi2 p={pc[2]:.2g}), OFC {fr[3]:.1f}% (p={pb[3]:.2g}, exact {px[3]:.2g}); "
          f"tests hold {tests} (exact {tests_x}), within 18 +/- 1.8 {within}")
print(f"tests hold with both fractions within tolerance under {nok} of {nrd} readings; with the exact test under {nok_x}")

Result: partially reproduced. The tests hold under several readings, the script's included (ACC 20.6% and DLPFC 17.9%, binomial p = 2e-14 and 3e-08, both above OFC by chi-square p = 6.8e-05 and 0.0016, OFC 6.0% at chance, p = 0.41), but in no reading computed here are both fractions within 18 +/- 1.8% with the tests holding: ACC is 20.6% in the script's reading, and where both fall within tolerance (19.0 and 18.7%, reading a, i, all trials, p < 0.05) OFC is above chance (10.4%, p = 0.0018). The tests hold in six readings with the scripts' binomial formula and in five with the exact test (reading b, iii, b, p < 0.05 fails it, DLPFC exact p = 1e-05); neither gives both fractions within tolerance. The significance flags the authors stored, from the same regression with their own permutations, give ACC 18.5% and DLPFC 17.2% with every test holding; they differ from the flags here in 2.1% of ACC units, so the difference is permutation noise around the threshold, but those flags are the paper's result, not one computed here.

fig8-spatial-value-dlpfc¶

In DLPFC, top/bottom spatial value neurons are as prevalent as left/right action value neurons, while in ACC they are significantly fewer, so DLPFC encodes value by spatial position and ACC by action.

In [57]:
nok = nok_x = nrd = 0
for key, alpha, k_, n_ in f8_all():
    pb = pfc7.binom_p_code(k_[2][3], n_[2], alpha)
    px = pfc7.binom_p_exact(k_[2][3], n_[2], alpha)
    pd_ = pfc7.chi2_yates(k_[2][3], n_[2], k_[2][1], n_[2])[1]
    pa_ = pfc7.chi2_yates(k_[1][3], n_[1], k_[1][1], n_[1])[1]
    rest = pd_ >= 0.05 and k_[1][3] < k_[1][1] and pa_ < 0.05
    ok = pb < 1e-6 and rest
    nrd += 1; nok += ok; nok_x += px < 1e-6 and rest
    print(key, f"DLPFC spatial {100 * k_[2][3] / n_[2]:.1f}% (binom p={pb:.1g}, exact {px:.1g}) vs action {100 * k_[2][1] / n_[2]:.1f}% "
          f"(chi2 p={pd_:.2g}); ACC spatial {100 * k_[1][3] / n_[1]:.1f}% vs action {100 * k_[1][1] / n_[1]:.1f}% "
          f"(chi2 p={pa_:.2g}) -> holds {ok}")
print(f"holds under {nok} of {nrd} readings; with the exact binomial test under {nok_x}")

holds under 2 of 26 readings; with the exact binomial test under 1

Result: reproduced, under 2 of 26 readings. With the full model, the 100-500 ms window, all trials and p < 0.01, DLPFC spatial value (8.2%, binomial p = 3e-08, exact 1e-07) equals action value (7.5%, chi-square p = 1), while in ACC spatial value (2.6%) is below action value (13.2%, p = 0.0003); the same holds with the value-only model (binomial p = 3e-07), which fails with the exact test (1e-06, not below the 1e-6 bound). In the script's reading the DLPFC binomial p is 2e-06, above the bound, with spatial 15.7% and action 17.9% (p = 0.74) and ACC 9.0% against 20.6% (p = 0.0024); the authors' stored flags give the same (binomial p = 7e-06).

figs9-ev16-correlation¶

The GLM's regressors of interest are decorrelated by design except EV 16, whose mean r2 with EVs 7 and 9 is 0.167 and 0.194.

The criterion uses trials with 3 or more cues; the GLM script computes DM_crosscorr before dropping trials with 2 cues, over all 724 units (shown as a variant over the units loaded here).

In [59]:
def r2mats(trials):
    out = {}
    for u, d in U.items():
        X = pfc7.glm_design(d)
        if trials == "3+":
            X = X[d["num_pics_viewed"] >= 3]
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            out[u] = np.corrcoef(X.T) ** 2
    return out
INT = list(range(0, 6)) + list(range(12, 18))
for trials in ("3+", "all"):
    R2 = r2mats(trials)
    by_sess = {}
    for u, m in R2.items():
        by_sess.setdefault((U[u]["sb"], U[u]["snum"]), m)
    for over, mats in (("sessions", list(by_sess.values())), ("neurons", list(R2.values()))):
        M = np.nanmean(np.stack(mats), axis=0)
        pairs = [(M[i, j], i, j) for i in INT for j in INT if i < j and 15 not in (i, j)]
        mx = max(pairs)
        print(f"trials {trials}, mean over {over} (n = {len(mats)}): r2 EV16-EV7 {M[15, 6]:.3f}, EV16-EV9 {M[15, 8]:.3f};"
              f" largest other pair among EVs 1-6 and 13-18: EV{mx[1] + 1}-EV{mx[2] + 1} {mx[0]:.3f}")

trials all, mean over sessions (n = 53): r2 EV16-EV7 0.190, EV16-EV9 0.211; largest other pair among EVs 1-6 and 13-18: EV3-EV15 0.013

Result: reproduced. Averaged over neurons on trials with 3 or more cues (reading b), the mean r2 of EV 16 is 0.180 with EV 7 and 0.190 with EV 9, within tolerance of 0.167 and 0.194, and the largest other pair among EVs 1-6 and 13-18 is 0.046. Averaged over sessions the values are 0.190 and 0.204, the first outside tolerance.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The data are the authors' preprocessed units and behavioural files of the data set, not the raw recordings. Where the claims file names readings, each was run, and the paper's scripts (files of the data set) settled the rest: the unit selection (the stored mean rate, unit 87 dropped, unit 653 dropped for Figures 5 and 7), the count of pictures viewed (joystick-corrected), the RSA conditions and permutation test, the projection design and reaction-time bins, and the cue 1 regression shown as a further reading for Figure 8. The GLM written here gives the T-statistics the authors stored in the data set to within 1.6e-06. The script's cue 1 regression gives the T-statistics stored in info_gathering_cue1_both.mat to within 3.3e-07, and the Figure 6 weights computed on the random halves the scripts stored equal the weights they stored to within 2.6e-07. Figure 6 is shown with the scripts' projection design and with the Methods' two-column projection, and with the action weights at -210 ms (scripts) and -200 ms (Methods). The data the projections use equal those the scripts stored in info_gathering_ramp_to_choice.mat for their first five random halves, apart from bins with one trial, which MATLAB's mean turns into a flat line in the script. The Figure 6 traces are not cut at each bin's longest reaction time, as the script does for plotting; the windows the criteria use lie before those cuts.

Revision after the first verification. figs5c-latency-order is now not reproduced (it was partially reproduced), as the criterion's test fails under every reading. Added: the Methods' projection and the -200 ms action bin for Figure 6, the scripts' stored random halves and halves shared within a session, the full 183 x 183 cross-correlation maps for Figure 5g-j with 8-connected clusters as in the script, the paper's n for the Fisher tests, the exact binomial test and the authors' stored flags for Figure 8, the per-session comparison with Supplementary Table 1, and the script lines the analysis cites.

Revision after the second verification. No outcome changed. Added: the t75 point estimates of every template for Supplementary Figure 5c, the single 183 x 183 map of Figure 5g-j with 10 other seeds and with 10000 permutations (under which it no longer passes for EV 3 with EV 2, so that outcome rests on the script's separate maps), and the check of the Figure 6 projected data against the scripts' stored data. Corrected: the t75 range, the Fisher p-value against ACC for EV 3 with EV 2, the count of Figure 8 readings under the exact test, and the rationale for the figs5c and figs1ab labels. The table marks the outcomes that hold under a minority of readings.

What was found about the data set. Its files hold what the paper describes: 25 and 32 behavioural sessions with the paper's trial counts, 549 units in the three regions over 24 and 29 sessions, every unit file agreeing with the units table on subject, session, channel and area, and the rasters on the clock of the trial events (the cue 1 value code rises after cue 1 and vanishes when trial labels are shifted by one trial). The mean rate that selects units (average_firing_rate in all_units_info.mat) is not documented and is not the whole-session or trial rate; unit files 681 to 724 (sessions 5, 11, 23 and 27 of M) store the subject as "m" where all others store "M"; and the data descriptor names the preprocessed folder LTH_preprocessed_data while the archive holds LTH_processed_data.zip. Supplementary Table 1 counts every unit of each session, although its caption says units above 1 Hz.
